newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative MP warns Clarke over budget.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative MP warns Clarke over budget.

text.p: British Conservative MP Nicholas Winterton threatened on Monday to vote against Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's budget if it neglects capital spending on public buildings and transport projects.
Winterton, chairman of the Manufacturing and Construction Industries Alliance, said capital investment had a vital role to play for business.
"I warn the chancellor bluntly on this point," he said in remarks prepared for delivery to industrialists in Birmingham on Tuesday.

"If his budget and expenditure statement fail to deliver the commitment that I am looking for on transport infrastructure in particular, then I for one will consider most carefully whether this is a budget that I could support in the lobbies."

Winterton also asked Clarke to send a positive message to the housing sector. "Home ownership is a core value of Conservatism which Chancellors should promote, not penalise as I fear that they have done in the past," he said.
Press reports have speculated that transport and housing could bear the brunt of spending cuts in Tuesday's budget to make room for lower taxes.

The voice of potential rebel members of parliament such as Winterton has grown louder as Prime Minister John Major's majority has shrivelled. It is now down to one in the 651-seat House of Commons and is set to disappear altogether after the December 12 by-election for Barnsley East, a safe Labour seat.
